note: Pass with real caveats. (1) INSTRUMENT (Step 3b): the table is the 6-item State Hope Scale (Snyder et al. 1996), not a Snyder Adult/Trait Hope Scale -- the article's Materials section says 'Hope was evaluated using the six item short version of the State Hope Scale (SHS)' and the S1 Appendix footnote a expands SHS as 'State Hope Scale'. Confirmed against Table 1: the six deposit columns give M=4.2497 and Cronbach alpha=0.8416 against the published Hope row 4.25 / .84. Table name and dictionary Description are correct. (2) ADMINISTERED IN GERMAN; THREE OF SIX ITEMS SHIP IN GERMAN, THREE IN ENGLISH. The study translated the SHS into German itself ('The German version of this scale was derived by translating the original version of the State Hope Scale into German (including a retranslation for verification purposes)'), so no pre-existing German SHS is the administered wording. Only three of the six German sentences were ever published: the S1 Appendix prints the CPC-12 in German and its items 1-3 are SHS1, SHS4 and SHS5. In-scope sources were exactly the article, S1 Appendix (.s001 PDF) and S1 Dataset (.s002, a semicolon CSV with a bare header row and no labels of any kind) -- there is no other supporting file -- and the German for SHS2, SHS3 and SHS6 appears in none of them. So hope1, hope4 and hope5 carry the administered German in item_text with English in item_text_translated, while hope2, hope3 and hope6 take the 2026-09-01 fallback: English in item_text, item_text_translated empty, language=German on every row. That is the row-level signal the standard defines ('populated language + empty _translated is the signal that the base fields are NOT the administered wording'), so the three fallback rows are findable by the backfill query and the three real ones are not. text_source is recorded as the weaker of the two, translated_substitute. (3) ENGLISH SOURCE. All six English strings are the instrument's own original English. For hope1/hope4/hope5 they are transcribed from the study's own S1 Appendix 'CPC-12 Scale (English)' list, which reproduces Snyder's wording verbatim; for hope2/hope3/hope6 from Brindal, Bainbridge & Kakoschke (2026), Front Psychol, PMC12813144 (CC BY), whose Table prints all six items prefixed HOPE1..HOPE6, i.e. numbered. The two agree character for character on the three items they share except that the Frontiers table drops the comma in 'Right now, I see myself...'; the study's own comma is what ships. Nothing was normalised. (4) OPTIONS. The paper states only 'All scales were surveyed using a 6-point response format ranging from 1 = strongly disagree to 6 = strongly agree' and publishes no German anchors, so option_text carries that English at resp 1 and resp 6 and resp 2-5 are BLANK, not padded with their own numbers; option_text_translated is empty because the base field is already the only published rendering. Note this is a 6-point administration of a scale whose original form is 8-point (1 definitely false .. 8 definitely true). (5) instructions and section_prompt blank -- none published for this administration. Single trivial section_id. correct_response empty (attitude scale). (6) MAPPING: reconstructed, verified PARTIAL. data/lorenz_2016_psycap.py is a pure melt preserving the deposit's column names, so hope1..hope6 are bare ordinals and no data_labels exemption exists. (7) RIGHTS: nothing to quote, so nothing blocks. The State Hope Scale carries no findable licence fee, non-commercial clause or redistribution bar from Snyder or his co-authors; the searches run were for a Snyder State Hope Scale permission/copyright statement, and the only 'copyright' page that surfaced was for the different, dispositional Adult Hope Scale and 404s. Per the 2026-09-04 rule silence is permission, and per the ECR-R ruling the licence that governs is that of the source copied from: the German came from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS article and the English from that same article plus a CC BY Frontiers article. (8) FINDING FOR THE SIBLING TABLE, NOT ACTED ON HERE: Fig 1 of this paper also prints the self-efficacy loadings box by box (GSE4 .56, GSE6 .79, GSE10 .70) and the reproduced model gives efficacy1.4 = .557, efficacy1.6 = .790, efficacy1.10 = .700 with residuals .690/.376/.510 against the printed .69/.38/.51. Every in-scope source was fetched and read; the two residual gaps (the German wording of SHS2/3/6, and hope2 vs hope6) are properties of what the study published, not of access. note: Clean pass with three disclosed caveats, one of which is a correction to how the response values must be read. (1) STEP 3b -- WHICH OPTIMISM INSTRUMENT. The deposit holds TWO optimism blocks and the table name does not say which is which. Lorenz et al.'s Materials section names both: '(a) The affective valence of the orientation towards the future-questionnaire (Affektive Valenz der Zukunftsorientierung, AFF) [62] with five items ... (b) The revised German version of the Life Orientation Test (LOT-R) [63] with ten items (four filler items and three items respectively tapping the subscales optimism and pessimism)'. The block sizes settle it (optimism1 has 5 columns, optimism2 has 10) and Table 1 confirms it numerically: optimism1.1-.5 give M=4.827 / alpha=.819 against the published AFF 4.83/.82, while the six non-filler optimism2 columns give M=4.406 / alpha=.736 against the published LOT-R 4.41/.74. optimism2 is the LOT-R. The dictionary Description ('Second 10-item optimism battery (LOT-R-length, Study 1)') hedges on this and could now be corrected to name the LOT-R outright; that is a dictionary edit, not a defect in the data. (2) ITEMS 3, 7 AND 9 ARE STORED ALREADY REVERSE-CODED, and option_text is inverted for those three rows. The LOT-R's own manual (Glaesmer et al. 2008 Anhang: 'Die Items 3, 7 und 9 muessen zur Berechnung des Gesamtscores umkodiert werden') and Carver's own page ('Responses to "scored" items are to be coded so that high values imply optimism') both treat recoding as a scoring step; this deposit applied it before depositing. Evidence: the six scored columns as stored give alpha .736, reproducing the published .74, whereas recoding them as the manual directs gives alpha -0.015; and the pessimism columns correlate +0.266 on average with the optimism columns, which is impossible for raw pessimism items. So resp=6 on optimism2.3/.7/.9 means the respondent chose 'strongly disagree', and the shipped anchors say so. This is the burkert_2019_whoqol_bref / baka2023_bpnsf move -- anchors matched to the data, override disclosed -- not a transcription of what the questionnaire form printed. (3) TEXT IS CANONICAL-INSTRUMENT, NOT STUDY MATERIALS. The study's own S1 Appendix prints exactly one of these ten items (CPC-12 item 6 = 'LOT-R10' = 'Alles in allem erwarte ich, dass mir mehr gute als schlechte Dinge widerfahren.'). The other nine German items are transcribed from the Anhang of Glaesmer, Hoyer, Klotsche & Herzberg (2008), the German LOT-R the paper cites as [63]; that appendix's item 10 is character-for-character the same sentence the study prints, which is what ties the study's administration to that particular German version. The English in item_text_translated is the LOT-R as its own authors administer it (www.psy.miami.edu/faculty/ccarver/lot-r.html), so it is a parallel version rather than a translation of the German beside it -- the German item 5 reads 'In meinem Freundeskreis fuehle ich mich wohl' ('I feel comfortable among my friends') where the English reads 'I enjoy my friends a lot'. (4) OPTIONS: the paper states only 'a 6-point response format ranging from 1 = "strongly disagree" to 6 = "strongly agree"' and publishes no German anchors, so option_text carries that English at resp 1 and 6 and resp 2-5 are BLANK, not padded with their own numbers; option_text_translated is empty because the base field is already the only published rendering. Note the study replaced the LOT-R's own 5-point 0-4 format with this 6-point one, so the Glaesmer form's German anchors ('trifft ausgesprochen zu' ... 'trifft ueberhaupt nicht zu') are NOT what respondents saw and were deliberately not carried over. (5) instructions and section_prompt blank: no instruction text is published for this administration, and the Glaesmer form's instruction belongs to the 5-point version. Single trivial section_id; correct_response empty (attitude scale), so key_source is empty. This matches the sibling lorenz_2016_efficacy1 shipped in batch_087. (6) MAPPING: reconstructed and PARTIAL -- see verification_lorenz_2016_optimism2.csv and verify_lorenz_2016_optimism2.R. data/lorenz_2016_psycap.py is a pure melt preserving the deposit's column names, so the codes carry an ordinal and nothing else. Four independent routes pin the structure: the published M/alpha selects {1,3,4,7,9,10} as the scored set out of all 210 six-column subsets, 9.4x better than the runner-up; the correlation block structure selects {1,4,10} vs {3,7,9} out of all 10 partitions (within .394 vs cross .266, gap .128 against .070 for the next); the CPC-12 CFA identifies optimism2.10 as LOT-R item 10, reproducing the paper's published chisq 77.727 / df 50 / TLI .950 / CFI .962 / RMSEA .042 exactly and beating every rival column; and optimism2.5's mean of 5.10, the highest of the ten, matches the friends filler. NOT pinned: optimism2.1 vs optimism2.4, the order within {3,7,9}, and the order within {2,6,8}. (7) RIGHTS: nothing to block on, and both halves were checked separately from the deposit licence. The PLOS article and its S1/S2 files are CC BY 4.0. The English LOT-R's rights holders publish the full instrument themselves at www.psy.miami.edu/faculty/ccarver/lot-r.html with no fee, no non-commercial clause and no redistribution bar -- the only stated restriction on that page is scope of application, 'Please note that this is a research instrument, not intended for clinical applications', which is a caution about clinical use rather than a term governing reproduction. The German version's only rights marking is a bare copyright line on the article offprint, 'Heide Glaesmer et al. 16 (1), 26-31 (c) Hogrefe Verlag Goettingen 2008'. Bare copyright is expressly not a block under the 2026-09-04 quote tests, and there is no clause to quote, so silence is permission. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate verdict, table shipped. An unchanged retry would reach the same result; only a rights holder publishing a restriction that does not exist today, or a source appearing with per-item LOT-R statistics (which would lift the mapping from PARTIAL to VERIFIED), would change it.
public_note: This study was run in German. item_text is the German LOT-R wording the respondents read, taken from the published German version the paper cites (Glaesmer et al. 2008) -- one of the ten items is also printed verbatim in the study's own S1 Appendix, which is what ties the administration to that version -- with the scale authors' own English alongside it; the German and English LOT-R are parallel versions rather than sentence-for-sentence translations, so item 5 reads 'I feel comfortable among my friends' in German where the English reads 'I enjoy my friends a lot'. Two things about the response values. The three pessimism items optimism2.3, .7 and .9 are stored ALREADY REVERSE-CODED, so resp=6 on those three means the respondent chose 'strongly disagree' and the option labels shipped for them run the other way from every other item; this was established from the data (the six scored items as stored reproduce the paper's published alpha of .74, while recoding them as the LOT-R manual directs gives alpha -0.02), not from any statement in the deposit. And the study replaced the LOT-R's own 5-point format with a 6-point one and published only English endpoint labels for it, so options 2 to 5 carry no text. Which LOT-R item each of the codes optimism2.1 to optimism2.10 refers to is reconstructed rather than stated by the source: the reconstruction fixes the four filler items and the optimism/pessimism split and reproduces the paper's published confirmatory factor analysis exactly, but optimism2.1 and optimism2.4 are not distinguished from each other, nor are the members of {optimism2.3, .7, .9} or of {optimism2.2, .6, .8}.

Tested in verify_lu_2017_gad7.R over all 1296 wave-1 respondents: GAD_5 is the strongest correlate of PHQ_8, the PHQ-9's only psychomotor item (0.449 vs 0.246/0.300/0.292/0.304/0.337/0.254), and PHQ_8 is reciprocally GAD_5's strongest PHQ-9 correlate (0.449, next 0.433 for PHQ_7); GAD_6 is the strongest correlate of PSS_9, the PSS-10 anger item (0.321 vs 0.275/0.290/0.261/0.222/0.203/0.203). That pins GAD_5 (restlessness) and GAD_6 (irritability); it does not separate GAD_1/GAD_2/GAD_3/GAD_4/GAD_7, hence PARTIAL.
